message.reasoning_content: Richardson iteration x_{k+1} = x_k + (b - A x_k) converges since eigenvalues in (0, 2). Convergence factor |1-λ|, worst λ=0.03125 → factor 0.96875, 64 steps → 0.96875^64 ≈ 0.13... error reduction ~0.13 relative? Actually error reduces per mode by (1-λ)^steps. Worst mode relative error factor 0.96875^64 ≈ e^{-2.0} ≈ 0.135. That's within 0.08? No, 0.135 > 0.08 — but relative L2 error includes contribution of that mode to x. x component along smallest eigenvalue direction: rhs has norm 1, component random ~0.25 typical. Error along that mode = 0.135 * (rhs component)/0.03125 vs ||x||_2 ~ 1/sqrt(avg λ)... hard analytically. Just run probe.
